test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall be void?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 13 of the Indian Constitution ensures the supremacy of Fundamental Rights by declaring that any law inconsistent with or derogating from Fundamental Rights shall be void.
 
• The term "law" under Article 13 includes ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications, customs, or usages having the force of law.
 
• Article 13 applies to both pre-Constitution laws (laws existing before January 26, 1950) and post-Constitution laws.
 
• This Article empowers courts to review legislation and strike down laws that violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• It serves as the cornerstone of judicial review in India, a crucial tool for protecting citizens' rights from unconstitutional actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution and guarantee civil liberties to all citizens.
 
• They include rights like equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, providing a mechanism for citizens to challenge violations.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Judicial Review refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders.
 
• Article 13 is a foundational provision enabling judicial review in India.
 
• It ensures that laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are invalidated, safeguarding citizens' rights.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Constitution and Post-Constitution Laws:**
 
 
• Article 13(1) deals with pre-Constitution laws, declaring them void if inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 13(2) prohibits the state from making laws that infringe on Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Severability:**
 
 
• Under Article 13, if a part of a law violates Fundamental Rights, only that part is declared invalid.
 
• The remaining provisions of the law continue to be enforceable, provided they are separable and do not contradict the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Eclipse:**
 
 
• Pre-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are not entirely void; they are dormant and overshadowed by the Constitution.
 
• If the inconsistency is removed, the law can become operative again.
